messages:
pagerbot: INCIDENT ALERT • p99 spike on dedicated-eu3 pools (streaming). trigger: latency_slo_p99 >= 7s for 6m, affected routes: /v1/stream, /v1/chat/stream :rotating_light:
eli_sre: taking it (oncall). joining bridge. any customer hits known?
maria_prod: few support tickets reporting streaming stalls, 10 customers with >90% of requests seeing >2s tail. escalating to sales for impacted accounts.
eli_sre: ok starting quick triage. initial dashboard: dedicated-eu3 pool utilization 98%, queue depth ~2400, per-pool warmup success rate down to 40%. p95 ~ 1.3s, p99 ~ 8.2s.
josh_infra: seeing autoscaler wants to add nodes but warmup handshake failing repeatedly: 
```
Autoscaler: scaleup requested 3 -> 6
warmup: handshake timeout after 45s, attempt=4
gpu-init: nvlink probe failed, retry backoff 30s
```
eli_sre: interesting — warmup handshake + nvlink errors. streaming stalls align with new hotshot reservoir allocations. looks like new nodes are slow to register so requests pile up.
support_led: CS reports one high-rev customer (AcmeCorp) seeing 503-ish stalls on stream reconnects, intermittent partial responses. Customers expect <200ms p95.
maria_prod: noting SLA exposure for two enterprise customers, raising to PS.
infra-bot: Telemetry: kv-cache-miss-rate spiked 6x on dedicated-eu3 at 13:04 UTC. network-retransmit increased ~4x.
eli_sre: hypothesis: when autoscaler spins new GPUs, their kernel init or nvlink stage is failing causing warmup to stall -> queue backs -> tail latency climbs. mitigation plan: 1) temporarily increase priority pool capacity by borrowing from eu1 spare nodes 2) enable graceful degrade routing to smaller model variant for streaming 3) force-retry warmup with alternate driver flags. opinions?
josh_infra: can do 1) borrow: initiating cross-region borrow is non-trivial (network cost) but we have eu1 spare 2 nodes. I'll open an action: `infra borrow eu1->eu3 2nodes --temp`.
eli_sre: do it. meanwhile enable fallback route: `route: streaming -> model: redwood-small-v2 fallback` (20% traffic) to shed load.
maria_prod: please notify impacted accounts with ETA ~15-30m. I’ll draft a short note.
support_led: AcmeCorp notified, they want mitigation now.
eli_sre: quick commands I’m running: 
```
# force re-register stuck nodes
for NODE in $(list-nodes --region eu3 --state initializing); do ssh $NODE 'systemctl restart gpu-init && tail -n 200 /var/log/gpu-init.log' & done
# temporarily route fallback
route update streaming --region eu3 --fallback redwood-small-v2 --weight 0.2
```
eli_sre: observed one node re-register at 13:07 but kernel logs show repeated `nvlink timeout` at driver init. pushing a kernel flag `--nvlink-delay=10s` to retrigger warmup with longer probe.
josh_infra: flag pushed to node init script; forcing warmup probe retry. also opening scaling override to bypass autoscaler backoff: `autoscaler override --region eu3 --scale-to 8 --reason "incident 7141592653"`
infra-bot: autoscaler override accepted, scaling target set to 8; provisioning started. warmup attempts now 6 -> 9.
eli_sre: after override, queue depth fell from 2400 -> 900 over 4 minutes. p99 dropped to ~3.5s but still above SLO. continuing mitigation.
maria_prod: update sent to customers: short note about degraded streaming performance, we have mitigation in progress, next update in 20m.
support_led: AcmeCorp replied: thanks, please prioritize. assigned rep on call.
eli_sre: enabling kv-cache prewarm for new nodes to avoid coldpath: `prewarm-kv --nodes new --buckets 50% --timeout 90s`.
josh_infra: prewarm kicked off; initial success for 4/6 nodes. one node still failing with driver error.
eli_sre: fallback ramp to 40% while we stabilize. `route update streaming --fallback redwood-small-v2 --weight 0.4`
maria_prod: recommended we open CR to label these nodes with `suspect-nvlink` and exclude from autopool until patched.
josh_infra: agreed. isolating 1 failing node: `node quarantine NODE-342` and reimage. starting kernel upgrade to silent-fix nvlink probe. ETA ~18m.
infra-bot: metrics: p95 now 0.9s, p99 2.1s after routing fallback and scale override. streaming stall rate down 85%.
eli_sre: good. keep routing fallback in place until nodes healthy. next steps: 1) reimage failing node, 2) validate warmup success rate >= 95%, 3) remove autoscaler override and gradually drain fallback.
maria_prod: sending second customer update: mitigations reduced impact; ETA for full recovery 30m.
support_led: logged impacted customers and case IDs to internal tracker.
eli_sre: callouts for postmortem: - root cause: nvlink probe regressions during GPU init causing warmup handshake timeouts - contributing factor: autoscaler backoff logic extended retry windows causing slow scale-up - mitigation actions: prewarm KV, temporary cross-region borrow, fallback routing, autoscaler override, node quarantine and reimage.
josh_infra: opening hotfix PR to increase nvlink probe timeout and add better driver retry logging.
maria_prod: will schedule customer RCA sync with enterprise customers after PM completes.
eli_sre: moving to monitoring phase. last check: p99 trending to 0.6-1.1s and queue depth steady ~120. I'll close paging if stable for 15m.
pagerbot: INCIDENT RESOLVED • p99 back under SLO for 20m, queue drained. incident closed. :white_check_mark:
